## Overview

This document presents data to inform decisions on filtering and aggregating clinically actionable mutations. The data are primarily aimed at aggregations at the level of individual patients. The results are organized into three sections

1.  Part 1 shows results for LEVEL 2 actionable events as assigned by OncoKB. The most common mutations are described at the level of cancer type, gene, and amino acid change.

2.  Part 2 shows results related to mutation co-occurrence at the level of Level 1 and Level 2 events

3.  Part 3 shows data on read coverage data and how filtering on this metric could affect patient-level aggregation.

Results are restricted to a subset of cancer types that have 250 or more patients with actionable events.

# Aggregation of data by cancer type

Data split by OncoTree codes

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
cTypeLvl1Cnts <- perPatientOncoKBLevelSorted %>%
  dplyr::filter(isOncoKbLevel1 == 1) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ONCOTREE_CODE) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_Level1_patients=n()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_Level1_patients))
lvl1Thresh <- 250
cTypeThresh <- cTypeLvl1Cnts[cTypeLvl1Cnts$n_Level1_patients >= lvl1Thresh,]

cTypeRep <- perPatientOncoKBLevelSorted %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ONCOTREE_CODE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number()==1)

cTypeCnts <- perPatientOncoKBLevelSorted %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ONCOTREE_CODE) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_patients=n(),
                   ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_patients))


cTypeCntTbl <- cTypeThresh %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cTypeRep[,c("ONCOTREE_CODE","CANCER_TYPE","CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED")],by=c("ONCOTREE_CODE")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cTypeCnts,by=c("ONCOTREE_CODE")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(percActionable = 100*n_Level1_patients/n_patients,
                actionableEvents = paste0(n_Level1_patients, " (", round(percActionable, 1), "%)"))

#cTypeCntTblPerc <- two_group_count_percentage(cTypeCntTbl,"n_patients","n_Level1_patients")


outCntTbl <- cTypeCntTbl[,c("ONCOTREE_CODE",
               "CANCER_TYPE",
               "CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED",
               "n_patients",
               "actionableEvents")]
colnames(outCntTbl) <- c("OT code",
               "cancer type",
               "cancer type detailed",
               "number of patients",
               "actionable events")
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(outCntTbl, )
```

# Most common mutated genes for each cancer type

top five actionable genes for each cancer type

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false

geneCnts <- perPatientOncoKBLevelSorted %>%
  dplyr::filter(isOncoKbLevel1==1) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ONCOTREE_CODE,Hugo_Symbol) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_gene_mutated = n()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(ONCOTREE_CODE,desc(n_gene_mutated)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() < 6)

cTypeCntTbl <- cTypeThresh %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cTypeRep[,c("ONCOTREE_CODE","CANCER_TYPE","CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED")],by=c("ONCOTREE_CODE")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cTypeCnts,by=c("ONCOTREE_CODE")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(geneCnts,by=c("ONCOTREE_CODE")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(percActionable = 100*n_gene_mutated/n_Level1_patients,
                geneOfactionableEvents = paste0(n_gene_mutated, " (", round(percActionable, 1), "%)")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_gene_mutated))

outGeneTbl <- cTypeCntTbl[,c("CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED",
                            "Hugo_Symbol",
                            "geneOfactionableEvents")]
colnames(outGeneTbl) <- c("cancer type detailed",
                         "gene",
                         "count and perc of actionable events")
```

Top 20 most common actionable events by gene

```{r}
knitr::kable(outGeneTbl[1:20,], )
```

## Actionable mutation co-occurrence across OncoKB levles

```{r}
perOncoKBEvntCnts <- svCompiled %>%
  dplyr::rename(SequenceCenter = Center) %>%
  #dplyr::left_join(assayInfo,by=c("SEQ_ASSAY_ID_mod"="SEQ_ASSAY_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(isOncoKbLevel1=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel3=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_3" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevelAny=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2or1=(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" | ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2") & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Tumor_Sample_Barcode) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nLevel1Events=sum(isOncoKbLevel1),
                   nLevel2Events=sum(isOncoKbLevel2),
                   nLevelAnyEvent=sum(isOncoKbLevelAny))
  #dplyr::arrange(desc(isOncoKbLevel1),desc(isOncoKbLevel2or1),desc(isOncoKbLevelAny)) %>%
  #dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number()==1) %>%

oncoKBEventCnts <- perOncoKBEvntCnts %>%
  dplyr::group_by(nLevel1Events,nLevel2Events,nLevelAnyEvent) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_patients=n(),
                   percent_total=100*n_patients/dim(perOncoKBEvntCnts)[1],
                   event_counts = paste0(n_patients, " (", round(percent_total, 1), "%)")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_patients))
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(oncoKBEventCnts[1:15,], )
```

## Effect of coverage filtering on the rate of actionable mutations

To examine the impact of coverage we, calculate the tumor profiling coverage as the following: t_ref_count+t_alt_count. We tested to see the imapct of filtering out variants with a min coverage below 20 bp.

The count of variant events below 20bp of coverage was as follows:

```{r}
table(svCompiled$t_alt_plus_ref_count < 20)
```

This resulted in the following impact on actionable mutation count:

```{r}

perPatientOncoKBBeforeCoverageFilt <- svCompiled %>%
  dplyr::rename(SequenceCenter = Center) %>%
  #dplyr::left_join(assayInfo,by=c("SEQ_ASSAY_ID_mod"="SEQ_ASSAY_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(isOncoKbLevel1=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel3=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_3" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevelAny=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2or1=(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" | ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2") & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Tumor_Sample_Barcode) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(isOncoKbLevel1),desc(isOncoKbLevel2or1),desc(isOncoKbLevelAny)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number()==1) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

perPatientOncoKBAfterCoverageFilt <- svCompiled %>%
  dplyr::filter(t_alt_plus_ref_count > 20) %>%
  dplyr::rename(SequenceCenter = Center) %>%
  #dplyr::left_join(assayInfo,by=c("SEQ_ASSAY_ID_mod"="SEQ_ASSAY_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(isOncoKbLevel1=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel3=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_3" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevelAny=ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_" & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY),
                isOncoKbLevel2or1=(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_1" | ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY=="LEVEL_2") & !is.na(ONCOKB_HIGHEST_LEVEL_SUMMARY)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Tumor_Sample_Barcode) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(isOncoKbLevel1),desc(isOncoKbLevel2or1),desc(isOncoKbLevelAny)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number()==1) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
```
